objective.name: manage_devices.py
objective.purpose: Multi-device manager and oracle for iOS simulators and Android emulators, backed by a SQLite (WAL) database. Lists/resolves devices, boots/stops them with host-tuned perf flags, warms and bakes them (Android dexopt compile levels + default_boot snapshots), clones/renames AVDs, manages aliases and ordered loops, and samples host-side CPU load. No-arg behavior: argparse error — exactly one mutually-exclusive action is required.
objective.side_effects: Writes SQLite at .device-manager/devices.db (device state, aliases, compile levels, warmup/bake timings, host profile). Boots/kills iOS sims (xcrun simctl) and Android emulators (adb), saves default_boot snapshots, clones/renames AVD dirs on disk, records history/last-used rows, logs host CPU samples.
objective.language_packages: stdlib only (sqlite3, subprocess, argparse, pathlib, datetime, signal, os, re, random, shutil, time, platform)
host_requirements: macOS (xcrun/simctl/sysctl/open are macOS-only) for the iOS half and host profiling
Android SDK installed for the Android half
defined iOS sims and/or Android AVDs

switches.effect: List all sims + AVDs (RUNNING then AVAILABLE); -v dumps full TSV record
List only running / mid-boot devices
Resolve id/alias (incl. ios/android/last-ios/last-android) to a maestro device id; bare id to stdout, rich desc to stderr; marks last-used
Record id/alias as last-<platform> without stdout output (for manual qa:flow runs)
Print device platform (ios/android), offline (qa infers --platform from --sim)
Print a running Android emulator's screen mode (headless/windowed/unknown)
Dump warmup/bake/start/kill timings (When, Device, Event, Detail, Dur, CPU%, Load)
Start device(s) with host-tuned perf flags (-gpu swiftshader_indirect, -cores, -memory, -no-boot-anim, -no-audio)
Start headless (-no-window -read-only) + perf flags (CI; screenshots black, a11y asserts work)
Start with legacy windowed behavior (no perf flags)
Stop device(s) gracefully (simctl shutdown / adb emu kill, saving quick-boot snapshot)
Stop everything with narrated SIGQUIT (EMU_KILL_GRACE_S grace) then SIGKILL escalation
Boot + wait until responsive; record warmup timing + host CPU/load; exit 1 on boot timeout
Warmup + bg-dexopt-job (~20-30 min, Android-only) + save default_boot; compile_level=low
Warmup + compile speed-profile (~20-40 min) + save default_boot; compile_level=medium
Warmup + compile everything --compile-layouts (~40-90 min) + save default_boot; compile_level=hot
Clone Android AVD (ATD-ify): copy, re-point to ATD image, wipe userdata, bake; iOS not implemented (FIXME)
Clone Android AVD as-is (no ATD re-point, no bake)
Persist a running AVD's state as default_boot snapshot
Boot headless, apply safe optimizations (compile optional), save default_boot, halt; Android-only
Periodic host-side CPU sampling of running devices (default 10s); runs until Ctrl-C
Create a user alias (persists across device deletion)
Rename an AVD (moves dir + migrates DB refs) or a user alias; rejects internal aliases
Define a named ordered loop of ids/aliases (validated)
Advance loop cursor (ACID BEGIN IMMEDIATE); next id to stdout, aliases to stderr
With --list/--running: full per-device TSV (UDID, serial, compile_level, has_default_boot, timestamps, notes)

objective.required_arguments: Exactly one action from the mutually-exclusive group (e.g. --list, --resolve, --start, --kill, --warmup, --bake, --next, ...). No action -> argparse usage error.
objective.explicit_env_checks: true — reads MANAGE_DEVICES_DB (default .device-manager/devices.db), ANDROID_HOME / ANDROID_SDK_ROOT (default ~/Library/Android/sdk), EMU_KILL_GRACE_S (default 4s)

subjective.usual_invocation: Two modes: (a) called programmatically by qa.ts and bench_sims.zsh for fast offline lookups (--resolve, --kind-of); (b) run manually by the developer for device lifecycle work (list, start, kill, warm, bake, clone, loop). The bare-id-to-stdout / rich-to-stderr split is designed for the programmatic callers.
subjective.invocation_change_recommendation: Mostly fine — it is already switch/long-option driven. One concrete change (from project memory): the bake/warm family (--warm:*, --bake, --save-quickboot, -w) take a single ID; make them nargs='+' like -s/-k/-c so a whole SIMS set can be baked in one sequential call. The action set is large; an interactive subcommand (à la testctl inspect) for device selection could help manual use.
subjective.linux_changes_needed: Partial port. HARD blockers: xcrun/simctl (iOS) and sysctl-based host_profile (hw.logicalcpu/memsize/cpu.brand) are macOS-only; SOFT blocker: `open -a Simulator`. PORTABLE: adb/emulator/sdkmanager and all SQLite/argparse logic. A Linux port needs the iOS code paths gated off and a Linux host-profile shim (/proc/cpuinfo, nproc, /proc/meminfo); Android management is otherwise viable in a container.

macos_dependency.notes: True for the iOS half (xcrun/simctl) and host profiling (sysctl/open). The Android half (adb/emulator/sdkmanager) is Linux-portable.

subjective.typical_runtime: Most actions are fast (list/resolve/kind-of/start/kill: seconds; warmup cold boot ~10-40s iOS, ~1-4 min Android). The compile/bake family is inherently long.
subjective.slow_switch_warning: Yes. --warm:low ~20-30 min, --warm:medium ~20-40 min, --warm:hot ~40-90 min, --bake (boot + optional compile + snapshot), and --copy with an ATD image download are all well over 2 minutes by design. These should carry an up-front time estimate/confirmation like bench_sims does.
subjective.dry_run_recommendation: Yes — strongly. This is the most destructive script in the set (clones, renames, wipes userdata, kills, overwrites snapshots) and has no --dry-run. Add one that prints the planned filesystem/device mutations (and AVD paths affected) without performing them.
subjective.destructive_steps: Many: kills sims/emulators; strips lock files and deletes snapshot dirs on clone; copytree/move of AVD dirs with no rollback on partial failure; wipes userdata*.img on ATD-ify; overwrites ~/.android/avd/config.ini on rename/clone; SQLite writes (WAL-protected).
subjective.rewrite_language_recommendation: No. Python + sqlite3 stdlib is well-suited to a stateful oracle; the WAL/ACID design depends on it.
subjective.merge_recommendation: Keep standalone — it is the shared device oracle for both qa and bench_sims (more than one consumer), so it must not be folded into either.
subjective.rename_recommendation: Optional — could expose as `manage_devices` (drop .py) since callers invoke it by path; low priority and would touch qa.ts/bench_sims call sites.
subjective.relocate_recommendation: Keep in scripts/. It is core, frequently used by the runners, not a rarely-used helper.
subjective.improvement_suggestions: Add --dry-run; add nargs='+' to the bake/warm family so a SIMS set bakes in one call; add up-front time estimates/confirmation to the long compile actions; add rollback (or a transaction/temp-dir swap) around AVD clone/rename so a partial failure does not leave a half-migrated AVD; cache the host profile so sysctl is not re-run every invocation; add an OS guard + Linux host-profile shim to enable Android-only use in containers.
subjective.requirements_check_completeness: explicit and incomplete — env vars and device existence are handled, but several subprocess steps proceed without validating success (e.g. ATD image download), AVD clone/rename have no rollback on partial failure, and the Android boot timeout is a hard-coded 300s.
subjective.external_dependency_breakdown: Scoring policy (v1.0): +1 per env var; +1 per non-standard / separately-installed program (xcrun/simctl, Android SDK tools, maestro, grpcurl, psql, gmtool, node/npm, lnav, etc.); programs shipped with macOS (ps, lsof, top, pgrep, sysctl, open, pbcopy, curl, osascript, system_profiler, git, grep/sed/awk) are NOT counted; +5 if a simulator/emulator is required on the primary path; +10 per large non-default app required (Xcode, Android Studio/SDK, Genymotion, Postgres, brew). Here: env 3 + programs 5 (xcrun, simctl, adb, emulator, sdkmanager) + sim 5 + apps 20 (Xcode 10 + Android SDK 10) = 33. (Ubiquitous ps/pgrep/top/sysctl/open no longer counted; down from 38 under v0.9.)
subjective.change_score_rationale: Weights (v1.0): Linux portability full-block +8 / partial +4 / portable 0; other dimensions +1 (or +2 where noted). Linux partial +4 (iOS hard-block, Android portable). Invocation (nargs='+' for the bake/warm family) +1. Missing --dry-run on a highly destructive tool +2. Destructive-without-rollback (clone/rename partial failure) +1. Gating incomplete +1. No tests +1. Total 10.
subjective.quality_score_rationale: Anchored rubric (v1.0), sub-scores sum to 100 — Error-handling/robustness /25: 19; Tests /20: 0 (no self-tests); Structure/clarity /20: 18; Documentation /15: 13; Portability + explicit requirement checks /20: 12. Total 62. Excellent SQLite WAL/ACID oracle and graceful kill ladder; docked for no rollback on partial AVD clone/rename, some unchecked subprocess steps, a hard-coded boot timeout, and no tests on a 2000-line stateful tool.
